comicPanels.title: Delivery Mission Initiated

patterns.title: The work never started.
patterns.description: System failed before initial action could begin.

patterns.title: The work started but stopped.
patterns.description: An unexpected halt interrupted execution midway.

patterns.title: The work finished but produced the wrong result.
patterns.description: All actions completed to the end, but the final outcome differed from physical expectation.

reflections: The measurement values were combined as text digits rather than adding physical quantities.
The scale sensor sent data before boxes settled on the platform.
The calculation rule applied the wrong mathematical operator.

pythonCode.codeSnippet:
val1 = "10"
val2 = "5"
total = val1 + val2
print("Total weight:", total)
pythonCode.buggyCode:
val1 = "10"
val2 = "5"
total = val1 + val2
print(total)
pythonCode.fixedCode:
val1 = 10
val2 = 5
total = val1 + val2
print(total)

storyComparison.storyText: Robot scale displayed '105kg' when 10kg and 5kg boxes were placed together.
storyComparison.pythonText: val1 = "10" and val2 = "5" join together as text "105" instead of adding numbers 10 + 5.

case1.expectedBehavior: Combine 10 and 5 as numeric addition to equal 15.
case1.hint: Look at lines 1 and 2. Are the numbers wrapped in quotes ("10") or plain numbers (10)?

bugFix.solution: Remove the quotation marks around 10 and 5 so Python adds them as numbers.

learningSummary.definition: The program runs completely without crashing, but produces an incorrect result because the calculation rule is wrong.
learningSummary.realLifeConnection: The robot scale displayed '105' because two text digits were stuck together instead of adding physical weights.
learningSummary.pythonConnection: Quotes around numbers ('10') make Python treat them as text strings. Removing quotes allows mathematical addition.
learningSummary.memoryTip: Logical errors don't crash your code—they just give wrong answers!
learningSummary.summarySentence: Quotes around numbers caused text concatenation instead of numeric addition.

patterns.title: The work never started.
patterns.description: System failed before initial action could begin.

patterns.title: The work started but stopped.
patterns.description: An unexpected halt interrupted execution midway.

patterns.title: The work finished but produced the wrong result.
patterns.description: The timer ran completely, but the winner ranking rule produced an unexpected output.

reflections: The ranking system treated higher time numbers as better scores.
The finish gate sensor swapped lane identities.
The timer display rounded the numbers incorrectly.

pythonCode.codeSnippet:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time > blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)
pythonCode.buggyCode:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time > blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)
pythonCode.fixedCode:
red_time = 8
blue_time = 12
is_winner = red_time < blue_time
print("Red wins:", is_winner)

storyComparison.storyText: Red Car finished in 8s (faster), but Blue Car (12s) was awarded the trophy.
storyComparison.pythonText: The comparison operator > checked for bigger time instead of smaller time.

case2.expectedBehavior: Evaluate 8 < 12 as True so the faster car wins.
case2.hint: In race timing, a faster car has a SMALLER time. Check the operator sign on line 3.

bugFix.solution: Change red_time > blue_time to red_time < blue_time.

learningSummary.definition: The code executes smoothly, but the comparison condition produces an unexpected result.
learningSummary.realLifeConnection: In a race, lower time means faster speed. The scoreboard used > instead of <.
learningSummary.pythonConnection: 8 < 12 evaluates to True, but 8 > 12 evaluates to False.
learningSummary.memoryTip: In race timing, smaller numbers win!
learningSummary.summarySentence: Using > instead of < declared the slower car as the winner.

storyComparison.storyText: The electronic display froze instantly before showing student report cards.

learningSummary.definition: Python cannot read or execute the program because a punctuation or grammar rule was broken.

learningSummary.memoryTip: Syntax errors crash before the code even starts running!
learningSummary.summarySentence: Missing colon (:) on the if statement caused an immediate Syntax Error.
